title: A Wreck for the Provision
premise: Freya Amberdale, estranged from her archaeologist father and drowning in debt to a river-town lender, accepts a dying prospector's map in exchange for a promise: carry it upstream to the glacier's forbidden source before calving season opens—and seals—the route. Pursued by the prospector's ruthless former partners and shadowed by a disgraced surveyor who knows the river better than anyone alive, Freya discovers the map leads not to gold but to her father's lost expedition camp. At the source, Freya must choose between the treasure that would erase her debt and the truth about why her father vanished—choosing the truth, she loses the fortune but gains a found family among the crew who carried her there.
about_author: Theo Vane is the pen name of a former river guide who spent six seasons running freight through glacial headwaters before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people who owe more than they own.

chapters.title: The Weight of a Promise
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. In the mud-flat town of Corrow's Landing, Freya digs salvage from the riverbed to chip at their debt. A dying prospector, Halloway, crawls into their camp and trades a grease-stained map for a sworn promise. Emotional beat: reluctant obligation; Freya takes the map mostly because refusing a dying man costs nothing—yet.

chapters.title: Debt Collectors and Dead Men
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The lender's enforcers come collecting, and Freya flees with only the compass and map, discovering Halloway was murdered for it. Two of his old partners, the Voss brothers, are already hunting the paper. Emotional beat: fear hardening into resolve; survival now requires going upstream, not hiding.

chapters.title: A Surveyor with Nothing Left to Lose
chapters.summary: Ilsa Brandt's POV. Disgraced surveyor Ilsa Brandt recognizes the map's hand-drawn markings—she charted that river years ago before being blamed for a disaster that wasn't hers. She intercepts Freya, offering passage on her leaky boat in exchange for a share. Emotional beat: wary alliance between two people who trust no one.

chapters.title: Upstream Against Everything
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The journey begins: rapids, portages, and the first glimpse of the glacier country. Ilsa teaches Freya to read water while the Voss brothers gain behind them. Emotional beat: grudging competence growing into something like respect; the river becomes a character, indifferent and demanding.

chapters.title: What Halloway Buried
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. In an abandoned trading post, they find Halloway's hidden journal: the map marks his betrayal—he sold out an expedition years ago and has been running from it since. The expedition's name is one Freya knows intimately. Emotional beat: dread; the promise is pulling Freya toward a past they've spent a lifetime avoiding.

chapters.title: The Voss Brothers Close In
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Ambushed at a canyon narrows, Freya and Ilsa barely escape when a third traveler, young deckhand Tam, creates a diversion and joins them. The Vosses take the boat; the trio must go overland. Emotional beat: loss and improvisation; the found family forms out of necessity, each member carrying a wound.

chapters.title: The Calving Window
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Racing the season, they reach the glacier's toe as ice groans overhead. A shortcut through the moraine nearly kills them, and Tam confesses he's been sending word to the Vosses to protect a sibling they hold hostage. Emotional beat: betrayal and forgiveness colliding; trust survives on terms, not innocence.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. At the forbidden source, they find the lost expedition camp—and Freya's father's final letters: he stayed behind voluntarily, sealing the site to protect it, and died believing his child would understand someday. The Vosses arrive with guns. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into clarity; Freya finally understands what belonging cost their father.

chapters.title: Ice and Gunpowder
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Climax. As the glacier calves, Freya triggers a controlled collapse that buries the treasure vault forever, destroying the map's value and the Vosses' claim. In the chaos, Tam frees himself of his blackmailers, and Ilsa saves the very men who ruined her—proving she's more than her disgrace. Emotional beat: sacrifice as victory.

chapters.title: Downstream, Together
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Resolution. The debt remains, but Freya returns to Corrow's Landing with Ilsa and Tam, negotiating honest work salvaging the river they now know better than anyone. Freya reads their father's last letter aloud at his memorial cairn. Emotional beat: quiet belonging; family isn't inherited—it's chosen, paid for, and kept.
